name: Riccardo Giacconi
summary: Nobel laureate physicist who founded X-ray astronomy and directed major observatories.

name: University of Milano
summary: Italian university where Giacconi completed his thesis in elementary particle physics.

name: University of Indiana
summary: US university where Giacconi worked on a Fulbright Fellowship.

name: American Science and Engineering
summary: Research company in Cambridge, Massachusetts where Giacconi started X-ray astronomy.

name: NASA
summary: US space agency that funded Giacconi's satellite programs.

name: Harvard University
summary: University where Giacconi became a Professor and moved his group.

name: Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory
summary: Observatory reorganized into the Center for Astrophysics with Harvard.

name: Space Telescope Science Institute
summary: Institute Giacconi directed starting in 1981.

name: European Southern Observatory
summary: Observatory Giacconi directed during VLT construction.

name: Associated Universities, Incorporated
summary: Corporation Giacconi became President of in 1999.

name: Bruno Rossi
summary: Physicist who suggested Giacconi look at X-ray observations of celestial objects.

name: Herbert Gursky
summary: Collaborator at ASE responsible for detectors.

name: Sco X-1
summary: First extrasolar X-ray source discovered by Giacconi's team.

name: Uhuru
summary: X-ray astronomy satellite launched in 1970.

name: Einstein Observatory
summary: X-ray telescope launched in 1979.

name: Chandra
summary: X-ray telescope launched in 2001.

name: Hubble Space Telescope
summary: Space telescope operated by STScI.

name: Very Large Telescope
summary: Optical ground-based telescope complex at ESO.

name: Atacama Large Millimeter Array
summary: Millimeter array project Giacconi was involved in.

name: Nobel Prize in Physics 2002
summary: Award shared by Giacconi for discovery of cosmic X-ray sources.

name: Genoa
summary: City in Italy where Giacconi was born.

name: Cambridge
summary: City in Massachusetts where ASE was located.
